newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government to submit tax code by April 30.
newsitem.headline: Russian government to submit tax code by April 30.

text.p: The Russian government will submit the final sections of a new tax code to the State Duma lower house of parliament by April 30, Deputy Finance Minister Sergei Shatalov said on Friday.
International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus has said that submitting the code to the Duma is a condition for the IMF releasing money to Russia from its $10 billion three-year loan.
"We have been given three days to finish working on it," Shatalov, responsible for tax reform in the ministry, told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
"The president has set April 30 as the limit, and I think we will make it."
Shatalin said the government believed the tax code would be passed by parliament this year, allowing it to come into force in 1998.
Foreign investors and Russian businessmen regularly complain about the present unwieldly and contradictory tax system which is enforced arbitrarily.
The current tax system prevents many businesses from opening up, and encourages many others to evade taxes altogether, aggravating Russia's financial crisis.
